page.title: Pool
page.purpose: Show how many ready takes exist per style, who is holding what, and when replenishment will run — so a consumer can tell whether a track is available right now without generating one.

priorities.statement: Depth per style is the headline number, because it answers the only question the page exists for: is a track available now?
A reserved take names its holder. A take missing from the pool must never be unexplained.
Replenishment is legible: whether it has been triggered, whether a batch is in flight, and that it runs on consumption rather than on a clock.
An empty pool is an ordinary state, not an error. The page says what it costs to fill it and what the caller can do meanwhile.
The storage cost of holding surplus is visible, because the budget is sized for discarded takes and that is easy to forget.

claims.statement: Each configured style shows its available and reserved counts against its target depth.
A reserved take identifies who is holding it and since when.
The page states whether replenishment is triggered, in flight, or blocked.
Low depth with no batch in flight surfaces the reason rather than appearing as ordinary low depth.
An empty pool states the cost of filling it and what is available meanwhile, rather than presenting as a failure.
The storage held by pooled takes is shown against its declared budget.
